stories.title: BIP-110 Bitcoin fork splits the chain, then stalls after two blocks
stories.summary: The contested BIP-110 soft fork moved into mandatory signaling with reported miner support below 3%, and Bitcoin briefly split into two chains after block 961,632. The branch enforcing BIP-110 mined only two blocks before stalling, with reports describing a silent miner boycott starving it of further blocks as the gap to the main chain widened.
stories.whyItMatters: A live, if short-lived, chain split shows how little consensus a controversial protocol change can command and underscores the coordination risk any future contentious Bitcoin upgrade carries.
whatToWatch: Whether the BIP-110 branch resumes mining or is effectively abandoned
Miner support levels for BIP-110 in coming days
Any exchange or node-operator guidance on which chain to treat as canonical
questions: What specifically does BIP-110 change, and why did it draw a boycott rather than broad adoption?
Is this split fully resolved or could the minority chain persist?

stories.title: Wall Street's $7B tokenized-fund pile sees under 1% actually used in DeFi
stories.summary: Institutional investors have put roughly $7 billion into tokenized funds, but according to a CryptoSlate report, less than 1% of that value is actively deployed within DeFi protocols. The bulk of the tokenized assets appear to sit largely idle rather than being used as on-chain collateral or in yield strategies.
stories.whyItMatters: It's a reality check on the tokenization narrative: institutional money is showing up on-chain, but the promised composability with DeFi hasn't materialized at scale yet.
whatToWatch: Whether tokenized-fund issuers build more direct DeFi integrations
Growth in on-chain usage rates for tokenized treasury and fund products
questions: What's the specific barrier keeping tokenized fund holders out of DeFi — regulatory, custody, or lack of demand?

stories.title: Bitcoin miner burned 357 BTC on undisclosed compute deals as output fell
stories.summary: A major Bitcoin mining company reportedly spent 357 BTC on compute-related deals that weren't previously disclosed, even as its Bitcoin production output dropped sharply, according to CryptoSlate. The report ties the spending to a broader trend of miners diversifying into AI/compute infrastructure.
stories.whyItMatters: Miner economics and transparency directly affect network hashrate and security, and investors in public mining companies rely on disclosed spending to assess whether a miner's core business is deteriorating.
whatToWatch: Whether the miner discloses further details on the compute deals
Next production/output reports from the company
Any investor or regulatory reaction to the disclosure gap
questions: Which miner is involved, and were these deals disclosed to shareholders through any other channel?
Is the output decline temporary or a sign of a broader pivot away from mining?

stories.title: Bitcoin spot ETFs pull in $853M, with BlackRock's IBIT leading inflows
stories.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs took in a combined $853 million in fresh inflows, with BlackRock's IBIT accounting for the bulk of the total, according to CoinDesk. The inflow marks a notably strong single-period showing for the ETF category.
stories.whyItMatters: ETF flows are one of the clearest real-time gauges of institutional demand for Bitcoin exposure, and concentration in IBIT continues to reinforce BlackRock's dominant role in the market.
whatToWatch: Whether inflows continue at this pace in subsequent sessions
Flow trends at competing issuers relative to IBIT
questions: What's driving the inflow spike — is it tied to a specific price move or catalyst?

stories.title: Brazil's central bank orders up to 24-hour delay on crypto transfers abroad
stories.summary: Brazil's central bank has directed crypto exchanges to hold large transfers sent abroad for as long as 24 hours, a measure aimed at curbing crypto-related fraud, per CoinDesk and Cointelegraph. The rule targets outbound transfers specifically rather than all crypto activity.
stories.whyItMatters: It's a concrete example of a major emerging-market regulator using transaction friction, rather than outright bans, to police crypto fraud — a model other regulators may watch.
whatToWatch: How exchanges implement the hold and whether it affects transfer volumes
Whether other jurisdictions adopt similar delay-based fraud controls
questions: What transfer size or transaction type triggers the mandatory hold?

stories.title: Crypto 'audited' badges may give investors false confidence, report warns
stories.summary: A CryptoSlate report argues that smart-contract 'audited' badges are increasingly used as a marketing signal rather than a genuine safety guarantee, potentially misleading investors about a project's actual risk. The piece raises concerns that audits vary widely in scope and rigor.
stories.whyItMatters: Retail and institutional investors alike often treat an audit badge as a green light, so gaps between audit marketing and actual security coverage directly affect fraud and exploit risk in DeFi.
whatToWatch: Whether exchanges or platforms start requiring standardized audit disclosures
Any incidents involving previously 'audited' protocols
questions: What specific audit practices does the report say fall short, and which firms are named?

sources.title: Why crypto ‘audited’ badges are giving investors a dangerous false sense of security

stories.title: Bitcoin's 'anti-spam' BIP-110 fork halts after mining only two blocks
stories.summary: The BIP-110 soft fork, pitched as an anti-spam measure for Bitcoin, ground to a halt after producing just two blocks, according to Decrypt. The stall follows the fork's attempted activation amid reportedly thin miner backing.
stories.whyItMatters: A high-profile Bitcoin protocol change failing to gain traction so quickly is a signal of how difficult it is to push contentious changes through Bitcoin's miner-driven consensus process.
whatToWatch: Whether BIP-110 proponents attempt another activation push
Any statements from Bitcoin Core developers or major mining pools on the outcome
questions: Is this fork attempt now considered dead, or could it resume?

stories.title: Bitwise's Solana ETF pulled in $267M, but market losses wiped out the gains
stories.summary: Bitwise's Solana ETF attracted $267 million in investor inflows, but according to CryptoSlate, market losses on the underlying position erased those gains entirely. The result leaves investors in the fund roughly flat despite the strong inflow figure.
stories.whyItMatters: It illustrates that ETF inflow headlines can mask underlying price weakness in the asset itself — a distinction that matters for anyone judging demand for altcoin ETF products.
whatToWatch: Whether inflows continue despite the negative price performance
Solana's price trajectory relative to the fund's cost basis
questions: Over what time window were the $267 million in inflows measured?

stories.title: AI financial advisers show a hidden Bitcoin bias, report claims
stories.summary: A CryptoSlate report says some AI-based financial advisory tools carry a latent bias toward or against Bitcoin that can be triggered by a specific prompt or setting. Details on which tools and how the bias manifests are limited in the report.
stories.whyItMatters: As more retail investors lean on AI tools for portfolio guidance, undisclosed biases in those systems could skew allocation advice around crypto without users' knowledge.
whatToWatch: Whether AI advisory platforms respond to or dispute the findings
Any follow-up testing of other AI tools for similar bias
questions: Which AI tools were tested, and what exactly is the 'switch' that triggers the bias?

stories.title: Is the CLARITY Act's delay actually good news for crypto?
stories.summary: CoinDesk's State of Crypto column examines whether the delay of the CLARITY market-structure legislation could ultimately benefit the industry rather than hurt it. The piece is framed as analysis rather than a report of new regulatory action.
stories.whyItMatters: Market-structure legislation is the biggest pending piece of the US regulatory puzzle for crypto, and how its timeline unfolds affects exchange compliance planning and institutional participation.
whatToWatch: Any new timeline or markup schedule for the legislation
Reactions from industry groups or lawmakers to the delay
questions: What specifically caused the delay, and what's the argument for it being beneficial?

stories.title: Saylor says ChatGPT helped Strategy unlock $15 billion for Bitcoin buys
stories.summary: Michael Saylor has said that ChatGPT played a role in helping Strategy structure a path to unlock $15 billion for its Bitcoin acquisition strategy, according to CryptoSlate. Specifics of how the AI tool was used weren't detailed beyond Saylor's account.
stories.whyItMatters: Strategy remains one of the largest corporate Bitcoin holders, so any change in how it finances further purchases is closely watched by the market as a demand signal.
whatToWatch: Whether Strategy deploys the $15 billion into further Bitcoin purchases
Any additional detail from Saylor or Strategy on the financing structure
questions: What financial mechanism did ChatGPT reportedly help identify or structure?

stories.title: Controversial Bitcoin fork BIP-110 mines two blocks, then stops
stories.summary: CoinDesk reported that the controversial BIP-110 Bitcoin soft fork managed to mine two blocks before activity on it stopped. The report is an early account of the fork's stalled activation attempt.
stories.whyItMatters: Even a brief, failed fork attempt highlights the difficulty of pushing disputed protocol changes through Bitcoin's consensus mechanism without broad miner buy-in.
whatToWatch: Whether mining on the BIP-110 branch resumes
Follow-up reporting on miner support levels
questions: Was this a permanent halt or a pause pending more miner support?
